newsitem.title: USA: PanEnergy deal shortens utility target list.
newsitem.headline: PanEnergy deal shortens utility target list.

text.p: Duke Power Co's $7.7 billion stock acquisition of PanEnergy Corp lifted the leading candidate off the short-list of natural gas companies ripe for merger with electric utilities.

Unless a competing offer emerges for the Houston-based natural gas company, electric utilities vying to be players in the convergence of the energy industry will be left jockeying to merge with eight or ten strong gas firms, analysts said.
"I think they are all going to go, eventually," said Salomon Brothers analyst Donald Dufresne, who placed Williams Cos Inc at the top of his list of merger targets.
Joining Williams on the analysts' short lost were KN Energy Inc, Consolidated Natural Gas Co, and El Paso Energy Corp once it digests its acquisition of Tenneco Energy.

NGC Corp, Equitable Resources Inc and Coastal Corp were also considered marger candidates, and traders said a hot takeover market could even spark a run at Enron Corp, the leading non-regulated electric wholesaler and only gas company to acquire a utility with its $3.2 billion deal for Portland General Corp.

Domestic utilities vying to be players in a deregulated nationwide power business are seeking strategic mergers with natural gas marketers, while others are merging with neighboring utilities in defensive move to protect their turf.

"Supermarket is the wrong word, but the right direction. There will be a guy selling electricity, natural gas and options, someone who will supply you with all your energy needs," First Albany analyst Mike Smolinski said.

Buying interest in Williams delayed opening of the stock, which was up 3-1/2 at 56 in midafternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange. NGC moved up 3/4 to an all-time high 20-3/4, and KN Energy hit a 52-week high before easing back to 40-1/2, up 2-1/8 on the Big Board.
